object.title: Thomassé's 8-edge-connected antisymmetric 5-flow conjecture
object.statement: Let $\vec{G}$ be a directed graph. An **antisymmetric $B$-flow** is a $B$-flow in which no two arcs receive inverse elements of $B$; in particular, it is nowhere-zero when $0=-0$. **Thomassé's conjecture.** Every directed $8$-edge-connected graph has a $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow. The source presents this as an open conjecture, motivated by the dual relationship with homomorphisms of planar graphs and by the existence of directed $7$-edge-connected graphs without a $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow.
object.source_name: Louis Esperet, Rémi de Joannis de Verclos, Tien-Nam Le and Stéphan Thomassé, “Additive bases and flows in graphs”, arXiv:1701.03366 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.03366

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2017).

object.title: Derangement excedance conjecture for the Chow groups of the generic Specht matroid
object.statement: Let $M(2,1^{n-1})$ be the Specht matroid associated with the partition $(2,1^{n-1})$, and let $A^k(M(2,1^{n-1}))$ denote its degree-$k$ Chow group. **Derangement excedance conjecture.** The dimension of $A^k(M(2,1^{n-1}))$ is the number of permutations in $S_n$ with no fixed points and $k+1$ excedances. This conjectural interpretation of the tabulated Chow-group dimensions was suggested with the help of OEIS sequence A046739; it remains open.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

object.title: The convex-extension conjecture for COM tope graphs
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_{\rm COM}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\rm OM}$ denote the classes of tope graphs of complexes of oriented matroids and oriented matroids, respectively. A graph $G$ is a **convex subgraph** of a graph $G'$ if $G$ is an induced subgraph containing every shortest path in $G'$ between vertices of $G$.

**Convex-extension conjecture.** Every $G\in\mathcal{G}_{\rm COM}$ is a convex subgraph of a graph $G'\in\mathcal{G}_{\rm OM}$.

This restates a conjecture from the cited literature in terms of tope graphs. It asks whether every COM tope graph can be embedded convexly into an oriented-matroid tope graph; the supplied text does not indicate that the conjecture has been resolved.

object.title: Aharoni–Kotlar–Ziv matching conjecture for regular simple tripartite 3-graphs
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $r$-regular simple $3$-partite $3$-graph with $n$ vertices in each class. **Aharoni–Kotlar–Ziv conjecture.**

$$
\nu(\mathcal{H}) \geq \frac{r - 1}{r}n.
$$

This conjecture concerns the matching number of simple regular tripartite $3$-graphs. For $r=n$, it generalizes the open Ryser–Brualdi–Stein problem on Latin transversals, and the conjecture is therefore likely to be difficult in full generality.
object.source_name: Penny Haxell and Lothar Narins, “A Stability Theorem for Matchings in Tripartite 3-Graphs”, arXiv:1701.06451 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06451

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2017). “These conjectures for $r = n$ generalize a notorious old open problem of Ryser-Brualdi-Stein on Latin transversals, so in their full generality they are likely to be very difficult.”

object.title: Armstrong's characteristic-polynomial conjecture for the Tesler poset
object.statement:
Let $U_n$ be the set of $n\times n$ upper-triangular matrices with non-negative integer entries. For $A=(a_{i,j})\in U_n$, define its hook sums by

$$
h_k:=\left(a_{k,k}+a_{k,k+1}+\cdots+a_{k,n}\right)-\left(a_{1,k}+a_{2,k}+\cdots+a_{k-1,k}\right).
$$

Let $\mathcal{T}(1^n)$ be the set of matrices whose hook sums are all $1$, and let $P(1^n)$ be the Tesler poset on this set. Its characteristic polynomial is

$$
\chi(P(1^n);q)=\sum_{A\in P(1^n)}\mu(\hat{0},A)q^{\rho(P(1^n))-\rho(A)}.
$$

**Armstrong's conjecture.** The characteristic polynomial satisfies

$$
\chi(P(1^n);q)=(q-1)^{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the enumerative structure of the Tesler poset and was attributed to Drew Armstrong. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Jason O'Neill, “On the poset and asymptotics of Tesler Matrices”, arXiv:1702.00866 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00866

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

object.title: The TM-MDS conjecture on generic nonsingularity
object.statement: Let $M$ be an $m\times n$ binary matrix satisfying the MDS condition. Let $N=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\}$ be independent indeterminates, let $V=V(N)$ be a generic $m\times n$ Vandermonde matrix with parameters $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$, and let $T=T(M,N)$ be a generic $m\times m$ transformation matrix such that $TV$ fits $M$. A matrix is **generically singular** when its determinant, viewed as a multivariate polynomial in $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$, is identically zero. **TM-MDS conjecture.** If $M$ satisfies the MDS condition, then $T(M,N)$ is not generically singular. The conjecture is equivalent to the GM-MDS conjecture through generalized Reed--Solomon constructions, but was open in the source.
object.source_name: Anoosheh Heidarzadeh and Alex Sprintson, “An Algebraic-Combinatorial Proof Technique for the GM-MDS Conjecture”, arXiv:1702.01734 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01734

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2017). “Despite all the attempts by the coding theory community, this conjecture remains still open in general.”

object.title: Vertex/facet trade-off conjecture for 2-level polytopes
object.statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional **2-level polytope**, meaning that every facet-defining hyperplane of $P$ has all vertices of $P$ on at most two parallel hyperplanes. Write $f_0(P)$ for the number of vertices and $f_{d-1}(P)$ for the number of facets.

**Vertex/facet trade-off conjecture.** One has

$$
f_0(P)f_{d-1}(P)\leq d2^{d+1}.
$$

Moreover, equality is achieved if and only if $P$ is affinely isomorphic to the cross-polytope or the cube.

This conjecture seeks a sharp bound on the product of the numbers of vertices and facets of a $d$-dimensional 2-level polytope. The bound is supported by experimental results through dimension $7$, but the source provides no resolution in general.
object.source_name: Manuel Aprile, Alfonso Cevallos and Yuri Faenza, “On 2-level polytopes arising in combinatorial settings”, arXiv:1702.03187 (2017).
object.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

object.title: Ultimate periodicity of Sprague–Grundy values along diagonals
object.statement:
Let $a_1$ and $a_2$ be nonnegative integers, and let $\mathcal{G}(a,b)$ denote the Sprague–Grundy value of the position $(a,b)$ in the game under consideration. **Diagonal ultimate-periodicity conjecture.** The sequence

$$
(\mathcal{G}(a_1+i,a_2+i))_{i \geq 0}
$$

is ultimately periodic.
The paper has established ultimate additive periodicity in each fixed row, but this conjecture concerns diagonals parallel to the main diagonal; its general validity is left open.
object.source_name: Graham Farr and Nhan Bao Ho, “The Sprague-Grundy function for some nearly disjunctive sums of Nim and Silver Dollar games”, arXiv:1702.07068 (2017).

object.title: The necessity of having no isolatable vertex for well-covered prisms
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected, triangle-free graph that contains a cycle of order $4$. The prism $G \Box K_2$ is the Cartesian product of $G$ with $K_2$, and a graph is **well-covered** if all its maximal independent sets have the same cardinality. An **isolatable vertex** is a vertex that belongs to an independent set whose removal leaves a graph with a unique perfect matching.

**Prism necessity conjecture.** If $G \Box K_2$ is well-covered, then $G$ has no isolatable vertex.

This conjecture proposes that, for connected triangle-free graphs containing a $4$-cycle, having no isolatable vertex is not only sufficient but also necessary for the prism to be well-covered. The supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
object.source_name: Bert L. Hartnell, Douglas F. Rall and Kirsti Wash, “On well-covered Cartesian products”, arXiv:1703.08716 (2017).
object.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

object.title: Generalized Zimin divisibility conjecture for formulas with reversal
object.statement:
Let $phi$ be a formula with reversal with $m$ two-way variables and $n$ one-way variables. Let $Z_{m,n}$ denote the corresponding Zimin formula with reversal. A formula is **unavoidable** if every sufficiently long word contains an instance of it.

**Generalized Zimin divisibility conjecture.** The formula $phi$ is unavoidable if and only if it divides $Z_{m,n}$.

The result is proved in the paper when there are at most two one-way variables; the conjecture asks for the corresponding characterization for any number of one-way variables.
object.source_name: James Daniel Currie, Lucas Mol and Narad Rampersad, “On avoidability of formulas with reversal”, arXiv:1703.10522 (2017).

object.title: Homogeneity and stationarity of universal quasi-flat models
object.statement:
Let $G\subset S_N^+$ be quasi-transitive, with all orbits of size $K$, and write $\Gamma=\widehat{G}$. Let $X_G$ be the universal quasi-flat model space and let

$$
\pi:C(G)\to M_K(C(X_G))
$$

be the corresponding model. **The virtual abelianity conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ satisfies a suitable virtual abelianity condition, then:

1. $X_G$ is a homogeneous space.
2. The model $\pi$ is stationary.

The conjecture is motivated by Thoma's theorem and explicit verifications, including the classical case. The paper notes that the relevant virtual abelianity condition is not yet defined in the quantum setting; in the classical case it requires an abelian subgroup of finite index. Thus the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Teodor Banica and Amaury Freslon, “Modelling questions for quantum permutations”, arXiv:1704.00290 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00290

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2017). “Thus, we will have here a solution to an old open problem.”

object.title: The period-determines-b2 invariant conjecture for 4-point c6^4 graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be $4$-point $c6^4$ graphs. Their Feynman periods are numerical invariants, and their $c_2$ invariants are graph invariants defined from point counts of the associated graph hypersurfaces.

**Period-determines-$c_2$ conjecture.** If $G$ and $H$ have equal periods, then they have equal $c_2$ invariants.

The conjecture expresses the expectation that the $c_2$ invariant is preserved by completion followed by decompletion and by the Schnetz twist, operations known to preserve the period. It remains open.
object.source_name: Iain Crump, “Graph Invariants with Connections to the Feynman Period in ϕ^4 Theory”, arXiv:1704.06350 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.06350

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2017). “It remains an open problem that the $c_2$ invariant is preserved by completion followed by decompletion and the Schnetz twist.”

object.title: Distinct symplectic-form values conjecture for non-collinear planar point sets
object.statement:
Let $E\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be a non-collinear point set, and let $\omega[E]$ denote the set of values of the symplectic form $\omega$ on all ordered pairs of points of $E$. Equivalently, these are the oriented areas of triangles with vertices the origin and two points of $E$. **Distinct symplectic-form values conjecture.** The cardinality of this set satisfies

$$
|\omega[E]|\gtrsim |E|.
$$

This is a planar distinct-values problem for non-degenerate bilinear forms. The source describes it as an open question; it notes that it is unclear whether the implicit comparison can be strengthened from $\gtrsim$ to $\gg$, and cites the best-known results without resolving the conjecture.
object.source_name: Misha Rudnev, “On distinct cross-ratios and related growth problems”, arXiv:1705.01830 (2017).
object.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

object.title: Strengthened conjecture for non-bipartite diameter-2-critical graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a non-bipartite diameter-$2$-critical graph of order $n$, and let $H_5$ be the exceptional graph and $\mathcal{C}_5^+$ the family of expanded $5$-cycles described in the source. **Strengthened conjecture.** If $G$ is not $H_5$, then $G$ has at most

$$
\left\lfloor(n-1)^2/4\right\rfloor+1
$$

edges, with equality if and only if $G$ belongs to $\mathcal{C}_5^+$ or is one of the thirteen graphs from Figure in the source.
This proposed strengthening removes the dominating-edge restriction and allows the thirteen displayed small graphs as additional equality cases; the supplied text does not establish the conjecture.

object.title: Sarkaria's non-embeddability conjecture for 2-complexes in four-space
object.statement:
Let $K$ be a $2$-dimensional simplicial complex, and let $f_i(K)$ denote the number of its $i$-simplices.

**Sarkaria's non-embeddability conjecture.** If

$$
f_2(K) \geq 4 f_1(K),
$$

then $K$ cannot be embedded into $\mathbb{R}^{4}$.

This conjecture concerns the extremal number of triangles in a complex embeddable in four-dimensional Euclidean space. The source attributes it to Sarkaria through Kalai's blog, but gives no resolution.

object.title: Monotonicity of worst-case bottleneck values for the $(\delta,k)$-PKRY algorithm
object.statement: For each $m$, let $S_m$ be a star with $m$ children rooted at its centre vertex, chosen to maximise the length of the longest edge in the tree produced by the $(\delta,k)$-PKRY algorithm, with every child at unit distance from the centre and no pair of children at distance less than $1$. Define $S_{m+1}$ similarly with $m+1$ children. Let $b$ and $b'$ be the bottleneck values of the outputs of $(\delta,k)$-PKRY on $S_m$ and $S_{m+1}$, respectively. **PKRY monotonicity conjecture.** Then $b \geq b'$. This is presented as a monotonicity property for worst-case arrangements, and the source describes it as a stronger version of an earlier conjecture; no proof or resolution is supplied here.

object.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig's combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
object.statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system, and let $u,v\in W$. The interval $[u,v]$ is the set of elements between $u$ and $v$ in the Bruhat order, and $P_{u,v}(q)$ denotes the classical Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial.

**Kazhdan–Lusztig's combinatorial invariance conjecture.** The polynomial $P_{u,v}(q)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of the interval $[u,v]$ as a poset.

This conjecture asks whether the classical Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial is determined by the abstract Bruhat interval, rather than by the Coxeter system and its labeling. It was independently formulated by Lusztig and Dyer; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

object.title: Equitable list arboricity conjecture for powers of paths
object.statement:
Let $n,p\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq p+1$, and let $P_n^p$ denote the $p$th power of the path $P_n$; that is, vertices at distance at most $p$ in $P_n$ are adjacent in $P_n^p$. Set $G=P_n^p$.

**Path-power equitable list arboricity conjecture.** The graph $G$ is equitably $k$-list arborable if and only if

$$
k\geq \left\lceil\frac{p+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The lower bound follows from the complete subgraph on $p+1$ vertices, while the supplied text says that the conjecture remains open for powers of cycles, not that this path-power conjecture itself has been resolved.
object.source_name: Hemanshu Kaul, Jeffrey A. Mudrock and Michael J. Pelsmajer, “On Equitable List Arboricity of Graphs”, arXiv:2008.08926 (2021).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1908.05066](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.05066), [arXiv:1809.08281](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.08281).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08926

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020). “Their conjecture is still open and is known as the Equitable $\Delta$-Coloring Conjecture.”

object.title: Taranenko's extension to positive permanents of polystochastic matrices
object.statement:
A **$d$-dimensional polystochastic matrix** of order $n$ is a nonnegative $d$-dimensional array whose entries on every line sum to $1$. Its permanent is the sum of the products selected by diagonals. **Taranenko's conjecture.** The permanent of every polystochastic matrix of odd order $n$ or even dimension $d$ is positive.

This statement is presented as an extension of Wanless's conjecture from multidimensional permutations to all polystochastic matrices. The source does not state that the extension has been resolved.
object.source_name: A. L. Perezhogin, V. N. Potapov, A. A. Taranenko and S. Yu. Vladimirov, “Characterization of polystochastic matrices of order 4 with zero permanent”, arXiv:2410.09546 (2024).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2303.17278](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17278), [arXiv:2004.14148](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.14148), [arXiv:1801.10306](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.10306).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09546

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “Despite Montgomery's recent breakthrough , proving that every latin square of large order $n$ has a near transversal (a partial transversal of length $n-1$), the Ryser's conjecture is still open.”

object.title: Simon's conjecture on extendable shellability of simplex skeleta
object.statement: Let $\Delta_{n-1}^{(d)}$ denote the $d$-skeleton of the $(n-1)$-dimensional simplex. A pure $d$-dimensional shellable complex on $n$ vertices is **extendably shellable** if every shelling of a subcomplex can be extended to a shelling of the entire complex. **Simon's conjecture.** The complex $\Delta_{n-1}^{(d)}$ is extendably shellable. Equivalently, any pure $d$-dimensional shellable complex on $n$ vertices can be extended to $\Delta_{n-1}^{(d)}$ by attaching one facet at a time while maintaining shellability. This conjecture concerns whether shelling sequences in simplex skeleta can always be completed; the source gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Rhea Ghosal, Melody Han, Benjamin Keller, Scarlett Kerr, Justin Liu, SuHo Oh, Ryan Tang and Chloe Weng, “Extendability of 1-decomposable complexes”, arXiv:2508.04555 (2026).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1911.12791](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.12791), [arXiv:1807.11012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04555

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).
